basic_info.about:
With over 20 years of experience as a tech entrepreneur and investor, I have built and scaled several successful companies and brands in the tech and D2C sectors, such as Shaadi.com, Makaan.com, and Mauj Mobile. I am the Founder & CEO of People Group, a well-renowned operator and investor in tech and D2C companies, including @Shaadi.com, the world's leading matchmaking company.

My mission is to create value and impact through innovation, technology, and customer-centricity. I am passionate about exploring new opportunities, supporting founders, and challenging the status-quo. I am also a Shark at Shark Tank India, where I invest in and mentor aspiring entrepreneurs. I have invested in over 200 tech and brand startups, ranging from Ola, Druva, Rupeek, Animall, Agnikul, FarEye, NxtWave, Quizzez, and several D2C companies like Skippi, Hair Originals, Zillionaire, & Whatsup Wellness. I am always looking for talented and driven people to join our team and our portfolio. You can reach out to me on Twitter @anupammittal or Instagram @anupammittal.me.

featured.description:
Your resume is going straight to the bin

If your resume looks like a government tender, don’t be surprised when it ends up in the shredder ✄

I see 100s of resumes and 95% are absolute junk. 
5 pages long, typos, Yahoo/Rediff IDs & photos? 😡

Bhai, bio-data nahin hai (uske liye Shaadi.com hai)

We all want the 50% hikes and fancy titles, but we don’t want to spend an hour figuring out how to write a good resume?

Kuch nahin toh, AI ko pooch lo 🤷🏻‍♂️

In India, we’ve become dangerously fatalistic. ‘Chalta hai’ dekhte hain’ 

No, it doesn’t work like that.
You have to try to shape the outcomes you want.

If you can’t put in the effort to create a compelling 1-page resume, why would anybody trust you with a job? 

The job of a resume is to get you an interview. Bas!

Unless you are trying to find a life-partner or doing a full KYC,
Get rid of that mug-shot, customize the resume to the role & co,
And fit it in 1 (2 if > 20 yrs) page. Simple.

I get called many things outside - founder, CEO, investor, super shark 🦈

At home, none of that survives the door.

Today Alyssa decided I needed decorating.
Some days it’s makeup💋Today it was Christmas 🎄

I don’t argue. I just sit there and enjoy it 💯 %

I’ve seen what happens when stress gets a seat at the table.
When kids inherit pressure they never signed up for.
Like many, I’ve been there 🤷🏻

I used to think I’d shift focus once I hit certain goals.

Funny thing - we chase ‘success’ for years
only to realize, it was also sitting at home, asking to be noticed.

So I decided - not anymore. Not in my house.

Bad days and bruised egos stay outside.
Inside, I’m Playful Papa. Sometimes Pyara Pati 😅

Haven’t cracked it fully but figuring it out, a day at a time.

Compliments of the season y’all ⭐♥️🤗

What’s with this 35% hike obsession? 🤷🏽‍♂️

Every time someone switches jobs in India, there’s this magic number - A 30-35% hike!

No logic. No context. Just ritual.

When asked why, the response is that it is ‘standard’. WTF? Who set this standard? I sure didn't get the memo 😅

💰Sure, you should earn your worth. But chasing a percentage hike every year is like running on a treadmill - a lot of motion, no progress.

The result?
Professionals who switch jobs every 12 months for a bump end up with no depth, no edge, and no real compounding.

If there’s one number worth chasing, it’s not a 35% raise. It’s a 35% 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡 𝐢𝐧 𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐫 𝐣𝐮𝐝𝐠𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 - in critical thinking, first principles thinking & creative problem-solving. 

Bcs everything else? It'll be automated by AI.

And when the market turns (and it always does), it won’t be the highest-paid who survives. It’ll be the ones who can produce, not output, but outcomes 💪🏽

When I joined MicroStrategy in Boston, they offered me $55K—way below the $80K market rate everyone else was pocketing 😅

Did I sulk? Negotiate? Complain? Nah😏

I felt shit but I took it.

📍 1 year later → I was in at HQ in DC helping build a new startup division from scratch.

📍 2 years later → Director of Strategic Partnerships ~ $200K + crazy stock options.

People kept asking—
"Bhai, manifest kiya? 

And you know what? Haan, thoda kiya😉

But → Manifestation only works when you match it with grind 😇

And yet, every few months, the 70-90 hour work week debate explodes online.

💀 “Hustle culture is toxic.”
💀 “Work smarter, not harder.”
💀 “My therapist said 30 hours max.”

Look, burnout is real. Balance matters. 

But let’s get one thing straight →
The best people don’t count hours. They align to outcomes. 


Here’s what I actually did -

1. Relentless, Disciplined, No-Excuses Work
No “ye uska kaam hai, ye mera kaam hai.”

If something needed doing—inside or outside my department—I did it. If I saw trash lying around, I picked it up.


2. I questioned everything

“Why are we doing this? Is there a better way?”

I was an employee, but I developed an ‘owners mindset’. I acted like I was building my own company. And that mindset changed my life. 



Aaj kal, I hear a lot of folks say ‘ye toh naukri hai, khud ka karenge toh josh se kaam karange’ 🙈

But ‘being an owner’ follows ‘taking ownership’ NOT the other way around.

So, here’s the cheat code ⬇️
Manifest like a baba. Work like a beast. Party like an animal 💪🏼

Warna zindagi hustle vs balance ke memes dekhte nikal jayegi😜

I had to make >800 applications and sit through 65 interviews before landing my first job.

Sounds insane but that was my reality when I graduated in the US - during a recession!

The job market was brutal, and every door seemed to be slammed shut—especially in the tech and VC industry, where I desperately wanted to work.

And unfortunately, I wasn’t from Harvard, Yale or Stanford or any other Ivy League.

I watched as others walked into jobs I knew I was capable of doing, and honestly, it drove me nuts. Every application, email, and interview hit a dead end.

But quitting was never on the table although I was dead-broke and finding it hard to make ends meet.

So, when Y2K came around and COBOL became a hot skill, I rolled up my sleeves & taught myself basic mainframe coding.

Eventually, landed an entry-level job as a COBOL programmer with Keane – I hated every minute of it 😥

Fortunately, just before I completely lost my mind, I got a call from MicroStrategy in Boston and was quickly hired as a pre-sales consultant.

But I knew the real action was in their Washington D.C. HQ. So, I took a shot in the dark and wrote directly to Michael Saylor the founder & CEO, asking for a role in their new venture Strategy.com

I got the role 😅 > Moved to D.C. > 2 years later, I was Director of Strategic Partnerships at a company that was the toast of Wall Street and darling of the tech world💪🏼

We went from a $100m to $40b mkt cap in that time. Yeah, let that sink in🚀

That job & my time in the US shaped me into who I am today🙏

But here’s the thing - this struggle wasn't just about landing a job- it was also about proving to myself that I was as good as the best.

To every struggler out there, the road is tough, but every "no" gets us closer to a yes, and that one "yes" has the power to change everything in our lives ✅

So, keep pushing, keep learning, and keep fighting for what you deserve coz our breakthroughs are out there. Sometimes they just need a little time to find us 🤗

Spent the day at a new-age B-school and it took me straight back to my own college days.

Met the students from @scalerschool_of_business, saw the products they’re building, and had some brilliant conversations. Left genuinely energised.

[MBA, Scaler School of Business, SSB]

We spend a lot of time asking whether education is keeping up with the world.

The more important question is: are young people getting close enough to real engineering problems, and getting exposure early enough?

My visit to @scaler_school_of_technology gave me a lot to think about. There’s a different kind of confidence that comes when students are encouraged to build & break things under the guidance of senior engineers who have been there and done that 💪🏼

Came back optimistic about what this generation is capable of. India needs more of this 🇮🇳

Visit the campus in Bangalore and see for yourself what this generation of engineers are already building.
